Viewing shared content requires Pro or Premium — but viewing your own My Workspace content is free.
Pinning tiles to a dashboard within My Workspace can be done on a Free account.

subtopic: Create and manage workspaces and assets
examObjective: Manage and secure Power BI > Lineage view
commonTrap: Confusing Lineage view with Relationships (model-level joins) or Connections (data source credentials) when the goal is to assess downstream impact of changing a shared semantic model
question: A Power BI administrator is planning a structural change to a shared semantic model and wants to first identify every report and dashboard that depends on it, so the impact can be assessed before making the change. Which option should the administrator use?
choices: Connections
Relationships
Lineage
Links
explanation: Lineage view in the Power BI Service shows the data flow between data sources, semantic models, reports, and dashboards. You can also use "Lineage - Impact analysis" to see what would be affected by changes.
choiceExplanations: Connections is not a workspace option for tracking report/semantic model relationships.
Relationships refer to data model table relationships, not Power BI Service content dependencies.
Correct. Lineage view shows the full dependency chain: data sources → semantic models → reports → dashboards.
Links is not a Power BI Service option for this purpose.

examObjective: Manage and secure Power BI > PowerPoint export
commonTrap: Assuming a saved-image embed must be redownloaded or reloaded to restore live data, rather than simply unchecking 'Show as Saved Image' in the add-in menu
question: A PowerPoint presentation contains an interactive Power BI report embedded by an analyst, who sent it to a recipient without a paid Power BI license by selecting 'Show as Saved Image'. The analyst now wants to make the report live again. What is the easiest way to do this?
choices: Click on the add-in slide menu and select "Reload".
Click on the add-in slide menu and un-check "Show as Saved Image".
You have to redownload the Power BI report into the PowerPoint presentation.
Click on the "Data options" menu and select "Reset".
explanation: Un-checking "Show as Saved Image" in the add-in slide menu re-enables the live interactive report. The report reloads and becomes live again without needing to redownload.
choiceExplanations: "Reload" is not an option in the add-in slide menu.
Correct. Un-checking "Show as Saved Image" restores the live interactive report.
You do not need to redownload — simply un-checking the image option restores the live connection.
"Data options" and "Reset" are not the correct menu path.

examObjective: Manage and secure Power BI > PowerPoint slicer behaviour
commonTrap: Assuming slicer selections made during a PowerPoint slide show persist after the show ends, rather than reverting to the state saved before the show started
question: A Power BI report contains a continent slicer. An analyst embeds it in PowerPoint with North America selected, then selects Europe before saving. During a slide show, the presenter clicks Asia, then Africa, and ends the slide show. What is currently selected?
choices: North America
Europe
Asia
Africa
explanation: When you end a PowerPoint slide show, all changes made during the presentation are reversed. The slicer reverts to the state it was in before the slide show started — which was Europe (selected after opening but before starting the show).
choiceExplanations: North America was the initial selection but was changed to Europe before the slide show started.
Correct. The slide show reverts to the pre-show state (Europe). Changes made during the show are discarded.
Asia was clicked during the slide show — those changes are reversed after the show ends.
Africa was the last click during the show — but slide show changes are discarded on exit.

examObjective: Manage and secure Power BI > PowerPoint live export
commonTrap: Looking for a live PowerPoint export under the visual-level Export menu or as an image embed, instead of using Share > PowerPoint > Open in PowerPoint to generate a live presentation
question: An analyst wants Power BI to generate a new PowerPoint presentation containing an interactive report directly from the Power BI Service. After opening the report, what should the analyst do?
choices: Go to Export - PowerPoint - Embed live data. Then click on Copy.
Go to Export - PowerPoint - Embed an image.
Click on the ... next to a visual, then go to Share - Open in PowerPoint.
Go to Share, then click on PowerPoint, then click on "Open in PowerPoint".
explanation: To create a new PowerPoint with a live interactive Power BI report, you go to Share → PowerPoint → "Open in PowerPoint". Power BI opens PowerPoint and creates a new presentation with the live report embedded.
choiceExplanations: Export - PowerPoint - Embed live data creates a copy in the browser, not a new PowerPoint file via the app.
Embed an image creates a static image, not an interactive report.
The ... on a visual opens visual-level options, not the full report export.
Correct. Share → PowerPoint → Open in PowerPoint creates a new PowerPoint file with the live interactive report.

examObjective: Manage and secure Power BI > Share link options
commonTrap: Expecting 'Allow recipients to share' or 'Restrict sharing' as the More options entry, when 'Manage permissions' is the option that opens the pane to view and modify all access permissions for the report
question: A user with a Power BI Pro license wants to share a report. After opening the report in the Power BI Service, the Send link dialog box appears, and the user clicks the ... (More options) button in the top-right corner. Which option is now available?
choices: Allow recipients to share this report
Manage permissions
Copy link
Restrict sharing
explanation: "Manage permissions" opens a pane where you can copy links giving access, change who has Direct access, and view/modify all permissions for the report.
choiceExplanations: "Allow recipients to share this report" is a checkbox in the Send link dialog, not in the ... menu.
Correct. The ... (More options) menu shows "Manage permissions" to control all access.
"Copy link" is already visible in the main dialog, not hidden behind ...
"Restrict sharing" is not a standard Power BI option name.

examObjective: Manage and secure Power BI > Test RLS in Service
commonTrap: Looking for a 'Test' or 'Run report' button after selecting a role, instead of using the ellipsis (...) menu next to the role name and selecting 'Test as role'
question: An administrator wants to test dynamic Row-Level Security in the Power BI Service using the Row-Level Security box, applying the MyRole security group. What should the administrator do?
choices: Select the MyRole and click the 'Test' button.
Select the MyRole and click the 'Run report' button.
Hover over the MyRole. Select the ... to the right of MyRole and select 'Test as role'.
Select the MyRole and click the 'Save' button. Then open the report and click 'Security' at the top.
explanation: To test a role in the Power BI Service, you hover over the role name, click the ... (ellipsis) that appears, and select "Test as role". This opens the report filtered as that role would see it.
choiceExplanations: There is no standalone "Test" button next to the role.
There is no "Run report" button in the RLS panel.
Correct. Hover over the role, click ... and select "Test as role" to preview the filtered report.
Saving and clicking Security at the top of a report is not how RLS testing works.

examObjective: Manage and secure Power BI > Test RLS in Desktop
commonTrap: Selecting a static role name or 'None' when testing dynamic RLS, instead of 'Other user' which lets you simulate a specific user's USERPRINCIPALNAME() value
question: A developer wants to test dynamic Row-Level Security in Power BI Desktop using Modelling - View as. Which role should be selected?
choices: None
Other user
RLS
Custom
explanation: "Other user" lets you enter the email address of a specific user or group. This is used for dynamic RLS where the USERPRINCIPALNAME() function filters data based on the logged-in user's email.
choiceExplanations: "None" applies no RLS role, so you would see all data.
Correct. "Other user" lets you enter a role email to simulate how that user would see data with dynamic RLS.
"RLS" is not a specific role option in the View as dialog.
"Custom" is not a role option in the View as dialog.

examObjective: Manage and secure Power BI > RLS DAX expression
commonTrap: Assuming an RLS filter expression like [PreviouslyOrdered] = TRUE() excludes or hides the matching rows, when RLS filters actually keep only rows where the expression evaluates to TRUE
question: A new role is created that uses the following DAX expression for the Customers table: [PreviouslyOrdered] = TRUE(). When this role is applied, what data would a user see?
choices: All customers who have previously ordered, as it filters those rows where the expression is true.
All customers who have not previously ordered, as it removes those rows where the expression is true.
All customers, regardless of whether they have previously ordered or not.
No customers — the expression excludes all rows.
explanation: An RLS DAX filter expression returns the rows where the expression evaluates to TRUE. [PreviouslyOrdered] = TRUE() filters to show only rows where the customer has previously ordered.
choiceExplanations: Correct. The RLS filter keeps rows where the expression is TRUE — customers who have previously ordered.
The filter keeps matching rows, not removes them. Rows where expression is TRUE are visible.
The filter expression limits the data — not all customers would be visible.
The expression filters TO matching rows, not away from them.
daxExpression:
-- RLS filter on Customers table: [PreviouslyOrdered] = TRUE()
-- This keeps rows where PreviouslyOrdered is TRUE
-- Users with this role only see customers who have placed an order before

examObjective: Manage and secure Power BI > Create RLS roles
commonTrap: Looking for RLS role creation under View, Insert, or in the Power BI Service dataset settings, instead of Modeling > Manage roles in Power BI Desktop
question: A Power BI developer needs to restrict report access so that each regional sales manager can see only the data for their own region. Before publishing the report, the developer wants to define a new security role with a DAX filter expression in Power BI Desktop. Where should the developer go to create this role?
choices: In Power BI Desktop, I go to View - Roles.
In Power BI Desktop, I go to Insert - Role.
In the Power BI Service, I go to the dataset, and click on "Security".
In Power BI Desktop, I go to Modeling - Manage roles.
explanation: RLS roles are created in Power BI Desktop under Modeling - Manage roles. You can then create roles, write DAX filter expressions per table, and assign columns. Role membership is managed in the Power BI Service.
choiceExplanations: View - Roles is not a valid menu path in Power BI Desktop.
Insert - Role is not a valid menu path.
The Power BI Service is where you assign users to existing roles — not where you create them.
Correct. Modeling - Manage roles is where you create and define RLS roles in Power BI Desktop.

examObjective: Manage and secure Power BI > Data alerts
commonTrap: Assuming data alerts can be configured on any dashboard tile, when alerts are only supported on tiles displaying a single numeric value (Card, KPI, Gauge) — not multi-value visuals like a pie chart
question: An operations manager wants to be notified by email whenever a key metric on their Power BI dashboard crosses a threshold, by configuring a data alert. The dashboard contains a Pie chart, a Card, a KPI, and a Gauge tile. On which of these tiles can a data alert NOT be configured?
choices: Pie chart
Card
KPI
Gauge
explanation: Data alerts can only be set on tiles that display a single numeric value: Cards, KPIs, and Gauges. Pie charts and other complex visuals are not supported for data alerts.
choiceExplanations: Correct. Pie charts cannot have data alerts — alerts are only supported on Cards, KPIs, and Gauges.
Card tiles support data alerts.
KPI tiles support data alerts.
Gauge tiles support data alerts.

examObjective: Manage and secure Power BI > Sensitivity label settings
commonTrap: Assuming sensitivity label policies can target specific individual users, when valid 'apply to' scopes are limited to the entire organization, specific security groups, or exceptions for specific security groups — not individual users
question: An organization wants to create sensitivity labels, but a user is not permitted to do so. An administrator enables this via Admin portal - Tenant settings - Information protection and must then choose who the setting applies to. Which of the following is NOT a valid 'apply to' setting?
choices: The entire organization
Specific security groups
Specific users
Except specific security groups
explanation: "Specific users" is not a valid target for sensitivity label permissions. You can apply to the entire organization, specific security groups, or exclude specific security groups — but not individual users.
choiceExplanations: "The entire organization" is a valid apply-to setting.
"Specific security groups" is a valid apply-to setting.
Correct. "Specific users" is not a valid option — you must use security groups or the entire organization.
"Except specific security groups" is a valid exclusion setting.

examObjective: Manage and secure Power BI > Pinned visual vs live page
commonTrap: Assuming a pinned visual tile updates to reflect later changes to the report, when only a pinned live page reflects the report's current state — a pinned individual visual remains a static snapshot
question: A report contains one table visual. An analyst pins the table visual and pins the live page to a new dashboard, then changes the table visual to a bar chart. Which of the following is true?
choices: The pinned visual will now be a bar chart. The pinned page will include a table.
The pinned visual will still be a table. The pinned page will include a bar chart.
The pinned visual will now be a bar chart. The pinned page will include a bar chart.
The pinned visual will still be a table. The pinned page will include a table.
explanation: A pinned visual is a static snapshot — it does not update when the report changes. A pinned live page is dynamic — it reflects the current state of the report page, including any visual type changes.
choiceExplanations: A pinned visual is static and retains the original type (table). A live page reflects changes.
Correct. The pinned visual stays as a table (static snapshot); the live page updates to show the bar chart.
The pinned visual does not update — it stays as a table.
The live page does update — it would show the bar chart after the change.

examObjective: Manage and secure Power BI > Subscriptions
commonTrap: Assuming a refresh-triggered subscription sends one email per refresh, when the maximum frequency for subscription emails is once per day regardless of how many times the data refreshes
question: A user subscribes to a report and configures the subscription to be emailed after the underlying semantic model has finished refreshing. The semantic model is scheduled to refresh 8 times per day. What is the MAXIMUM number of subscription emails the user will receive in a single day?
choices: One email per hour.
One email per day.
One email per week.
One email per month.
explanation: When set to trigger after data refresh, the maximum frequency for a Power BI subscription email is once per day, regardless of how many times the data refreshes.
choiceExplanations: Power BI subscriptions cannot send more than once per day.
Correct. The maximum frequency for subscription emails triggered after refresh is once per day.
Once per week is below the maximum frequency — daily is the maximum.
Once per month is below the maximum frequency.

examObjective: Manage and secure Power BI > Create dashboard
commonTrap: Looking to create a dashboard via Desktop upload, '+ Create', or directly from a semantic model, instead of pinning tiles from one or more existing reports or workbooks in the Service
question: A Power BI Service user has published several reports to a workspace and now wants to combine key visuals from two of those reports into a single at-a-glance view for executives. How should the user create this dashboard?
choices: You upload it from Power BI Desktop.
You directly create it from a semantic model in the Power BI Service.
You create it from one or multiple reports or workbooks in the Power BI Service.
You create it from going to "+ Create" on the left-hand side of the Power BI Service.
explanation: Dashboards are created by pinning tiles from one or more reports or workbooks in the Power BI Service. You cannot create a dashboard by uploading from Desktop or directly from a semantic model.
choiceExplanations: Power BI Desktop publishes reports, not dashboards.
You cannot create a dashboard directly from a semantic model.
Correct. Dashboards are built by pinning visuals from reports or parts of workbooks.
"+ Create" creates reports or other items — not the primary way to create dashboards.

subtopic: Configure a semantic model scheduled refresh
examObjective: Manage and secure Power BI > Incremental refresh
commonTrap: Using plausible-sounding but incorrect parameter names (RefreshStart/RefreshEnd, PeriodStart/PeriodEnd, SetStart/SetEnd) instead of the exact, case-sensitive RangeStart and RangeEnd required by Incremental Refresh
question: A semantic model connects to a large Sales fact table containing five years of transaction history. To reduce refresh time, a data engineer wants to configure Incremental Refresh so that only recent data is reloaded on each scheduled refresh while historical data remains cached. Before defining the refresh policy in Power BI Desktop, which two Power Query parameters must the engineer create (with these exact, case-sensitive names)?
choices: RefreshStart and RefreshEnd
SetStart and SetEnd
PeriodStart and PeriodEnd
RangeStart and RangeEnd
explanation: Incremental Refresh requires two Power Query parameters named exactly RangeStart and RangeEnd (case-sensitive), both with DateTime data type. These are used to filter the data source during incremental loads.
choiceExplanations: RefreshStart and RefreshEnd are not the correct parameter names.
SetStart and SetEnd are not the correct parameter names.
PeriodStart and PeriodEnd are not the correct parameter names.
Correct. RangeStart and RangeEnd (case-sensitive, DateTime type) are the required parameter names.

subtopic: Configure a semantic model scheduled refresh
examObjective: Manage and secure Power BI > Scheduled refresh options
commonTrap: Assuming scheduled refresh notifications can be configured for success or sent to arbitrary users, when the available option is specifically failure notifications sent to the dataset owner
question: A data engineer configures Scheduled refresh for a semantic model that powers a critical morning sales report. They want to be proactively alerted if the overnight refresh fails so they can fix it before the business day starts. Which of these is an available notification option when setting up the schedule?
choices: Send refresh success notifications to the dataset owner
Send daily notifications to the dataset owner
Send refresh failure notifications to the dataset owner
Email these users when the refresh succeeds
explanation: When configuring scheduled refresh, you can opt to send failure notifications to the dataset owner. This notifies them if the refresh fails so they can investigate and fix the issue.
choiceExplanations: Refresh success notifications are not a standard scheduled refresh option.
Daily notifications regardless of refresh status are not an option.
Correct. You can configure failure notifications to alert the dataset owner when a refresh fails.
Email on success is not a standard scheduled refresh notification option.

subtopic: Identify when a gateway is required
examObjective: Manage and secure Power BI > Data gateway
commonTrap: Assuming a gateway is needed for multiple data sources, shared semantic models, or manual refreshes, when a gateway is specifically required only when data resides on-premises
question: An analyst wants to refresh a semantic model that is in the Power BI Service. In which scenario would a data gateway be required?
choices: When you have multiple data sources in your dataset.
When at least some of your data is in your own premises network or computer.
When a semantic model is used by multiple reports.
When you want to manually update the semantic model.
explanation: A data gateway is required when your data resides on-premises (in a private network or on a local computer) and needs to be refreshed by the Power BI Service in the cloud. It acts as a secure bridge between cloud and on-premises data.
choiceExplanations: Having multiple data sources does not automatically require a gateway.
Correct. A gateway is needed when data is on your premises network or local computer — not reachable by the cloud directly.
The number of reports using a semantic model does not determine gateway requirements.
Manual refresh can be triggered from the Power BI Service without a gateway for cloud data sources.

subtopic: Promote or certify Power BI content
examObjective: Manage and secure Power BI > Endorsement levels
commonTrap: Choosing Certified (which requires admin-configured review) or invented endorsement levels like 'Advanced'/'Validated', when Promoted is the self-service endorsement that needs no certification review
question: An analyst wants to endorse a semantic model, but the endorsement does not need to be reviewed against the company's certification criteria. Which endorsement should be used?
choices: Advanced
Certified
Promoted
Validated
explanation: There are two endorsement levels: Promoted (can be set by the dataset owner, no review required) and Certified (requires an admin-configured review process to confirm quality standards are met).
choiceExplanations: Advanced is not a Power BI endorsement level.
Certified requires a review process — the question says no review is needed.
Correct. Promoted endorsement can be applied by the dataset owner without a formal review.
Validated is not a Power BI endorsement level.

subtopic: Create and manage workspaces and assets
examObjective: Manage and secure Power BI > Analyze in Excel
commonTrap: Expecting Analyze in Excel to open a pre-built table or report copy, rather than an empty PivotTable connected live to the semantic model's fields
question: A finance analyst wants to explore a published semantic model using familiar pivot-table tools rather than building a new Power BI report. They go to the semantic model in the Power BI Service and select 'Analyze in Excel'. When the Excel file opens, what do they see?
choices: A table, with the data
An empty PivotTable, so you can drag in the fields you want to show
An empty table, so you can drag in the columns you want to show
An analysis based on a report, which you can then alter
explanation: Analyze in Excel opens a connected Excel file with an empty PivotTable and the Power BI field list on the right. You then drag fields into the PivotTable to build your analysis.
choiceExplanations: The data is not pre-loaded into a flat table — you build the view yourself via PivotTable.
Correct. You get an empty PivotTable connected to the semantic model, ready for you to add fields.
PivotTable (not a flat empty table) is what appears — you drag fields, not columns.
The Excel file does not contain a pre-built analysis — it starts empty.

examObjective: Manage and secure Power BI > Publish to web
commonTrap: Confusing 'Publish to web' (public, internet-wide, admin-gated) with organizational embed or Power BI Embedded for ISVs, which serve internal or developer-licensed audiences rather than the general public
question: A marketing team wants to embed a Power BI report on a public website so that anyone on the internet can view it without signing in. When they try to publish the report, they find that this option is unavailable to them by default and must be enabled by an administrator. Which publishing option is this?
choices: Embed - Securely embed this report in a website or portal
Embed for your organization - share the report in an internal company portal
Generate an embed token through Power BI Embedded for ISVs
Publish to web - Embed this report for public access by anyone on the Internet
explanation: "Publish to web" creates a publicly accessible embed code that anyone on the internet can view. Because of security implications, it is disabled by default and must be enabled by a Power BI administrator in Tenant settings.
choiceExplanations: Secure embed is available by default for licensed users, but viewers must sign in — it does not provide anonymous public access.
Embed for your organization is available by default and only allows authenticated users within the company to view the report — it does not provide sign-in-free public access.
Power BI Embedded for ISVs requires a separate Azure capacity (A/EM SKU) and app registration set up by a developer — it is not a simple tenant setting an administrator toggles on.
Correct. "Publish to web" is off by default — it requires admin to enable because it makes content publicly available.

examObjective: Manage and secure Power BI > App permissions
commonTrap: Assuming app audience access is capped at a small fixed number of individual users or requires splitting into multiple apps, instead of granting access to a security group containing all intended recipients
question: An organization with 300 employees wants to create an app and share it with 200 specific individuals. What is the best way to do this?
choices: You can only have 100 users in an app, so you have to create two apps.
Create an app for 100 users, and then share what reports others need.
Create a group containing these 200 people, and use this group in the permissions section.
Give access to the Entire organization, and only send the link to the 200 individuals.
explanation: The recommended approach is to create a security group with the 200 people and grant the group access in the app permissions. This is scalable and maintains proper access control.
choiceExplanations: There is no 100-user limit for apps — you can share with much larger groups.
There is no 100-user limit and this is not the recommended approach.
Correct. Create a group of 200 users and assign the group in the app permissions section.
Giving Entire organization access would include the 100 people who should not have access.

examObjective: Manage and secure Power BI > Workspace roles
commonTrap: Assuming Member or Admin is required to create reports from existing datasets, when Contributor is the minimum role that allows this
question: Francis wants to access a workspace and create reports in this workspace based on existing datasets. What is the MINIMUM workspace role he needs?
choices: Admin
Member
Contributor
Viewer
explanation: Contributor role allows creating and editing content using existing datasets but not managing workspace settings or publishing apps. Member and Admin have broader permissions. Viewer can only view.
choiceExplanations: Admin has full control including managing members — more than required.
Member can publish apps and manage roles — more permissions than needed.
Correct. Contributor can create reports from existing datasets — the minimum required role.
Viewer can only view content — cannot create reports.

examObjective: Manage and secure Power BI > App visibility
commonTrap: Assuming only users explicitly granted app permissions can view it, when all workspace members (any role) automatically have access to apps published from that workspace
question: Brian and Chloe are working on a workspace — Brian is the Admin, Chloe is a Viewer. Brian creates an App and gives David permissions to see it. Who can view the App?
choices: David only.
Brian and David.
Brian, Chloe and David.
Brian only.
explanation: All workspace members (Brian and Chloe) automatically have access to the app because they have workspace access. David was explicitly granted permissions. So all three can view the app.
choiceExplanations: David has access, but so do workspace members Brian and Chloe.
Chloe also has access as a workspace member.
Correct. Workspace members (Brian and Chloe) automatically see apps from that workspace. David was explicitly added.
Brian is the only one mentioned here but Chloe and David also have access.

examObjective: Manage and secure Power BI > App limits
commonTrap: Assuming apps cannot contain dashboards or are limited to a very small number, when an app can include up to 200 dashboards
question: A workspace owner is packaging multiple dashboards and reports into a Power BI app for distribution to the sales organization. What is the maximum number of dashboards that can be included in a single app?
choices: Zero - they are not allowed in an App.
explanation: An app can contain up to 200 dashboards in addition to reports and other content.
choiceExplanations: Dashboards are allowed in apps.
1 dashboard would be too restrictive — the limit is 200.
20 is not the correct limit.
Correct. An app can include up to 200 dashboards.

subtopic: Create a narrative visual with Copilot
examObjective: Visualize and analyze the data > Copilot features
commonTrap: Looking for the Copilot 'Summarize this data' capability within the semantic model view or a dashboard, when it is accessed from within a Report in the Power BI Service
question: A Sales Director asks an analyst to use Copilot to generate a written summary of the trends in the underlying semantic model so it can be embedded as a narrative visual in a report. In which of the following locations should the analyst ask Copilot to summarize the semantic model?
choices: Semantic model
Report
Dashboard
Power BI Desktop
explanation: Copilot for summarizing the underlying semantic model is accessed from within a Report in the Power BI Service — not directly from the semantic model view or a dashboard.
choiceExplanations: Copilot for semantic model summarization is accessed from a Report, not the semantic model itself.
Correct. Copilot to summarize the semantic model is available within Reports in the Power BI Service.
Copilot is not available from Dashboard tiles.
Power BI Desktop does not have Copilot for semantic model summarization.

subtopic: Create a narrative visual with Copilot
examObjective: Visualize and analyze the data > Narrative visual
commonTrap: Confusing the Narrative visual (Copilot-generated text summaries) with other AI visuals like Key Influencers or Decomposition Tree, which provide AI-driven analysis but not Copilot-written narrative text
question: A report designer wants to add a visual that uses Copilot to automatically generate a written summary of the trends shown on the page. Which of the following visuals provides this Copilot-powered capability?
choices: Narrative
Key influencers
Decomposition tree
KPI
explanation: The Narrative visual uses Copilot to automatically generate text summaries and insights about the data in your report. Key influencers and Decomposition tree are AI visuals but do not use Copilot.
choiceExplanations: Correct. The Narrative visual leverages Copilot to generate natural language summaries of the data.
Key influencers is an AI visual but uses machine learning, not Copilot.
Decomposition tree is an AI visual for hierarchical exploration — not Copilot powered.
KPI is a standard visual, not powered by Copilot.

subtopic: Use Copilot to create a new report page
examObjective: Visualize and analyze the data > Copilot availability
commonTrap: Assuming Copilot for report creation is available only in Power BI Desktop, when Copilot in the Power BI Service is available within Reports to create pages and generate insights
question: An analyst wants to use Copilot in the Power BI Service to help create a new report page and generate insights about the underlying data. In which of the following areas of the Power BI Service is Copilot available for this?
choices: Semantic models
Reports
Dashboards
You can't - you can only use it in Power BI Desktop.
explanation: Copilot in the Power BI Service is available in Reports — you can use it to create report pages, summarize data, and generate insights. It is not available directly in the semantic model view or on dashboards.
choiceExplanations: Copilot is not available directly in the semantic model view.
Correct. Copilot is available in Reports within the Power BI Service.
Copilot is not available in the Dashboard view.
Copilot is available in the Power BI Service (Reports), not just Desktop.

subtopic: Use Copilot to create a new report page
examObjective: Visualize and analyze the data > Copilot Fabric capacity
commonTrap: Assuming F1 capacity or no capacity at all is sufficient to enable Copilot features, when a minimum of F2 Fabric capacity is required
question: An organization wants to enable Copilot features for report authors working in a Power BI Service workspace. What is the minimum Fabric capacity SKU that the workspace must be running on for Copilot to be available?
choices: F1
F2
You don't need a Fabric capacity.
explanation: Copilot in the Power BI Service requires a minimum of F2 Fabric capacity in the workspace. F1 is not sufficient for Copilot features.
choiceExplanations: F1 capacity is not sufficient for Copilot — the minimum is F2.
Correct. Copilot in the Power BI Service requires at least F2 Fabric capacity.
F64 would work but is far more than the minimum required.
A Fabric capacity (minimum F2) is required for Copilot in the Power BI Service.

examObjective: Prepare the data > Get or connect to data
commonTrap: Confusing 'Get Data' with 'Load Data'
question: An analyst is working in an existing Power BI Desktop file and needs to add a new data source — a SQL Server table — to the model alongside the existing tables. Which option should they use?
choices: Load Data
Get Data
Open Data
Find Data
explanation: In Power BI Desktop, 'Get Data' is the entry point for connecting to any data source. It is found on the Home tab.

choiceExplanations.0: 'Load Data' is not a menu option in Power BI Desktop. Data loading occurs automatically after selecting a source through Get Data.
choiceExplanations.1: Correct. 'Get Data' is the entry point in Power BI Desktop for connecting to any new data source, including SQL Server tables, and is accessed from the Home tab.
choiceExplanations.2: 'Open Data' is not a valid Power BI Desktop option. File > Open is for opening existing .pbix project files, not for connecting to new data sources.
choiceExplanations.3: 'Find Data' does not exist in Power BI Desktop. The only term used throughout the interface for connecting to data sources is 'Get Data'.

examObjective: Visualize and analyze the data > Create reports
commonTrap: Confusing Focus mode with Zoom mode
question: While reviewing a report page containing several visuals, an analyst wants to temporarily enlarge a single chart to fill the entire canvas, hiding the other visuals, so they can examine it in detail. Which icon should they click on the selected visual?
choices: Data mode
Focus mode
Zoom mode
Expand
explanation: Focus mode enlarges a single visual to fill the entire canvas. You can exit Focus mode by clicking 'Back to report'.

choiceExplanations.0: Data view is a workspace view in Power BI Desktop that shows raw table data — it is not a visual-level display feature and does not magnify individual visuals.
choiceExplanations.1: Correct. Focus mode enlarges the selected visual to fill the entire report canvas, hiding the other visuals so it can be examined in detail. Click 'Back to report' to exit.
choiceExplanations.2: 'Zoom mode' is not a named feature in Power BI Desktop. The correct feature name is 'Focus mode'.
choiceExplanations.3: 'Expand' refers to expanding hierarchy rows in a matrix or tree visual — it is not a visual enlargement or full-screen feature.

examObjective: Visualize and analyze the data > Create reports
commonTrap: Thinking the visual must be deselected first
question: A table visual has been added to an existing Power BI file. An analyst wants to change it to a stacked bar chart. What is one way of doing this?
choices: Ensure that no visual is selected, then go to Home - Insert - Stacked bar chart.
Ensure that no visual is selected, go to the Data/Fields pane, click on the fields, and select 'stacked bar chart'.
Ensure the visual is selected, and go to 'Build a Visual'/Visualization pane, and click on 'stacked bar chart'.
Ensure the visual is selected, and go to Data/Fields pane, and click on 'stacked bar chart'.
explanation: To change a visual type, the visual must be selected. You then go to the Visualization pane (Build a Visual) and click the desired chart type.

choiceExplanations.0: Inserting a chart from Home > Insert when no visual is selected adds a new visual to the canvas — it does not convert an existing table into a different chart type.
choiceExplanations.1: The Data/Fields pane shows available fields for drag-drop into visual sections — it does not contain chart type selection options, and with no visual selected any action creates a new visual.
choiceExplanations.2: Correct. To change a visual's type, the visual must first be selected, then a different chart type is chosen from the Visualization pane (Build a Visual) — this converts the existing table into a stacked bar chart while keeping its fields.
choiceExplanations.3: The Data/Fields pane manages which data fields are in the visual's sections — it does not contain options for changing the visual type.

subtopic: Create and manage workspaces and assets
examObjective: Manage and secure Power BI > Publish, import, or update items in a workspace
commonTrap: Thinking 'Share' or 'Upload' is the correct menu option
question: An analyst has finished building a report in Power BI Desktop and now wants to make it available to colleagues through a workspace in the Power BI Service. Which option should they use?
choices: File - Publish - Publish to Power BI
File - Upload - Upload to Power BI
File - Share - Share to Power BI
File - Move - Move to Power BI
explanation: To publish a report from Power BI Desktop to the Power BI Service, go to File > Publish > Publish to Power BI. You can also use the Publish button on the Home tab.

choiceExplanations.0: Correct. File > Publish > Publish to Power BI (also available via the Publish button on the Home tab) sends the report and its data model from Power BI Desktop to a workspace in the Power BI Service.
choiceExplanations.1: 'Upload' in Power BI Service allows importing a .pbix file via the browser — but from Power BI Desktop, the correct option is File > Publish > Publish to Power BI, not 'Upload'.
choiceExplanations.2: 'Share' is used in the Service to grant individual users access to specific reports — it is not a Desktop menu option for sending reports to the Service.
choiceExplanations.3: 'Move' is used in Power BI Service to relocate content between workspaces — it is not a publish mechanism available from Power BI Desktop.

examObjective: Prepare the data > Transform and load the data > Select appropriate column data types
commonTrap: Assuming Image is a valid data type because Binary is
question: A developer is reviewing column data types in Power BI Desktop's Model view before building relationships. Which of the following is NOT a valid data type that can be assigned to a field?
choices: Whole number
Image
Date/time
Text
explanation: Image is not a valid data type in Power BI. Valid types include Whole number, Decimal number, Fixed decimal number, Date/time, Date, Time, Text, True/False, and Binary.

choiceExplanations.0: Whole number is a valid Power BI data type — it stores integer values and is one of the most commonly used types.
choiceExplanations.1: Correct. 'Image' is not a selectable Power BI data type for fields. Valid types include Whole number, Decimal number, Fixed decimal number, Date/time, Date, Time, Text, True/False, and Binary.
choiceExplanations.2: Date/time is a valid Power BI data type that stores both date and time information and enables time intelligence functions.
choiceExplanations.3: Text is a valid Power BI data type for string values and is one of the core supported types.

examObjective: Visualize and analyze the data > Format and configure visuals
commonTrap: Going to the Data pane or Format pane instead of the Visualization pane
question: A visual displays 'Sum of SalesVolume'. An analyst wants to change the aggregation from Sum to Average for this visual only. How can this be done?
choices: Click on the field in the Data pane, and go to Column tools.
Select the visual, and go to the 'Build a visual'/Visualization pane.
Select the visual, and right-hand click on the visualization.
Select the visual, and go to the Format pane.
explanation: To change the aggregation for a specific visual, select the visual and go to the Build a Visual/Visualization pane. You can then right-click on the field or click the arrow next to it to change the aggregation.

choiceExplanations.0: Column tools changes the default aggregation for a field across the entire model — this affects all visuals using that column, not just the specific visual you want to change.
choiceExplanations.1: Correct. Selecting the visual and opening the Build a Visual/Visualization pane lets you change the aggregation (e.g., from Sum to Average) for just that field on that visual, without affecting the field's default aggregation elsewhere.
choiceExplanations.2: Right-clicking on the visual canvas does not expose aggregation settings — you must interact with the field inside the Visualization pane (Build a Visual) to change the aggregation per visual.
choiceExplanations.3: The Format pane controls visual appearance — colors, fonts, borders, backgrounds — and does not contain aggregation type options.

examObjective: Visualize and analyze the data > Format and configure visuals
commonTrap: Looking for a 'Copy Formatting' right-click option
question: Two visuals exist on a report page. The first visual has been fully formatted, and an analyst wants to copy that formatting to the second visual. How can this be done?
choices: Click on the first visual, select Home - Format Painter, and click on the second visual.
Click on the first visual, select Home - Format Special - Formats, and click on the second visual.
Click on the first visual, select Home - Copy, click on the second visual, and select Paste - Formats.
Right-hand click on the first visual, select Copy - Copy Formatting, and click on the second visual.
explanation: Format Painter in the Home tab allows you to copy formatting from one visual and apply it to another by clicking the target visual.

choiceExplanations.0: Correct. Format Painter, found on the Home tab, lets you copy all formatting from a selected visual and apply it to another visual by clicking that target visual.
choiceExplanations.1: 'Format Special > Formats' is not a real Power BI menu option. The Format Painter is the only built-in tool for copying visual formatting.
choiceExplanations.2: Copying and pasting a visual in Power BI duplicates the entire visual including data — it does not selectively paste only formatting onto a different existing visual.
choiceExplanations.3: Right-clicking a visual does not offer a 'Copy Formatting' or 'Copy Format' option. Format Painter in the Home ribbon is the correct and only built-in approach.

examObjective: Visualize and analyze the data > Create reports
commonTrap: Using double-click or right-click instead of Ctrl+click
question: A report designer wants to align two visuals on a report page so they are evenly spaced. After clicking on the first visual, how should they also select the second visual so that both are selected together?
choices: Double-click on the second visual
Right-hand click on this second visual
Hold down Control and click on the second visual
Hold down Alt and click on the second visual
explanation: Hold down Ctrl (Control) and click on the second visual to select both visuals simultaneously. You can also use Shift+click to select both visuals.

choiceExplanations.0: Double-clicking a visual enters edit mode for that visual (e.g., editing a text box or title field) — it does not add it to a multi-selection with the first visual.
choiceExplanations.1: Right-clicking a visual opens its context menu — it does not add it to a multi-selection alongside the first visual.
choiceExplanations.2: Correct. Holding Ctrl and clicking the second visual adds it to the current selection, allowing both visuals to be selected together for alignment or distribution actions. Shift+click also works.
choiceExplanations.3: Alt+click is not a multi-select keyboard shortcut in Power BI. The correct modifier key for multi-selection is Ctrl (Control).

examObjective: Visualize and analyze the data > Select an appropriate visual
commonTrap: Thinking Line and clustered bar chart is a standard single visual
question: A regional manager wants a single visual that shows monthly revenue as columns alongside a profit margin trend as a line, both on the same chart. Which of the following standard visuals in the Visualization pane provides this combination (note: this is one single visual, not two separate visuals)?
choices: Line and clustered bar chart
Line and pie chart
Line chart and table
Line and stacked column chart
explanation: The 'Line and stacked column chart' is a standard combined visual in Power BI. You can also use a 'Line and clustered column chart'. There is no built-in 'Line and pie chart' or 'Line chart and table' combined visual.

choiceExplanations.0: There is no 'Line and clustered bar chart' built-in combined visual in Power BI. Bar charts are horizontal — Power BI provides a 'Line and clustered column chart' (vertical columns, not horizontal bars) as the combined visual.
choiceExplanations.1: There is no built-in 'Line and pie chart' combined visual in Power BI — pie charts cannot be natively combined with a line chart into a single visual.
choiceExplanations.2: There is no built-in 'Line chart and table' combined visual — these two are always separate visual types in Power BI.
choiceExplanations.3: Correct. The 'Line and stacked column chart' (along with 'Line and clustered column chart') is a built-in combo visual that displays columns and a line series together on a single chart with shared and secondary axes.

examObjective: Visualize and analyze the data > Select an appropriate visual
commonTrap: Confusing stacked column chart with clustered column chart
question: A regional sales director describes a visual she sees in a report: "There are years from 2000 to 2016 across the bottom, Sales Volume on the vertical axis, and for each year there is a single bar divided into colored sections — one color per region — stacked vertically on top of each other." Which visual type does this description match?
choices: Clustered column chart
Stacked column chart
Clustered bar chart
Stacked bar chart
explanation: A stacked column chart shows vertical bars with segments stacked on top of each other, each segment representing a category (e.g., region). A clustered column chart would show separate bars side by side.

choiceExplanations.0: A clustered column chart shows separate vertical bars placed side by side for each category — the bars are NOT stacked on top of each other into one bar per X-axis value.
choiceExplanations.1: Correct. A stacked column chart displays vertical bars for each X-axis category (year), with each bar divided into colored segments stacked on top of each other representing the different regions.
choiceExplanations.2: A clustered bar chart shows horizontal bars side by side — the description shows vertical bars running upward from the X-axis, which are columns, not horizontal bars.
choiceExplanations.3: A stacked bar chart stacks horizontal bars end-to-end — the description shows vertical bars (columns stacked upward), not horizontal bars.

subtopic: Enhance reports for usability and storytelling
examObjective: Visualize and analyze the data > Configure drillthrough navigation
commonTrap: Thinking only the selected year expands, not all years
question: A matrix has the OrderDate hierarchy in the rows section and is currently showing the years 2023 to 2025. What happens if a user clicks on the year 2024, then clicks 'Expand all down one level in the hierarchy'?
choices: All of the years in the OrderDate field will be expanded to the Year and Month hierarchy.
All of the years in the OrderDate field will be expanded to the Year and Quarter hierarchy.
The 2024 year only will be expanded into months. The other years will remain as years.
Instead of showing OrderDate years, it will show Quarters instead.
explanation: 'Expand all down one level' expands ALL rows down one level in the hierarchy — not just the selected row. In a standard date hierarchy, below Year is Quarter, so all years expand to show quarters.

choiceExplanations.0: In the standard Power BI date hierarchy, the level below Year is Quarter — not Month. Month comes below Quarter. 'Expand all down one level' moves from Year to Quarter.
choiceExplanations.1: Correct. 'Expand all down one level' expands every row in the hierarchy by one level simultaneously, regardless of which row is selected. Since Quarter sits directly below Year in the standard date hierarchy, all years (2023-2025) expand to show Quarters.
choiceExplanations.2: 'Expand all down one level in the hierarchy' always expands ALL rows simultaneously — pre-selecting year 2024 does not restrict the expansion to that row only. To drill into a single row, use the drill-down arrows directly on that specific row.
choiceExplanations.3: When expanding down, both hierarchy levels (Year and Quarter) remain visible — the Year level does not disappear. Having only Quarters replace Years describes drill-down, which removes the parent level.

examObjective: Visualize and analyze the data > Select an appropriate visual
commonTrap: Thinking both table and matrix can summarise data
question: A report developer needs to display sales data with countries as rows and product categories as columns, showing individual cell values and row subtotals per country. A colleague suggests using a table visual. Which statement correctly identifies why a matrix visual is more appropriate for this specific layout requirement?
choices: A table can summarise data. A matrix cannot summarise data.
A table cannot summarise data. A matrix can summarise data.
A table has a fixed number of columns. A matrix has a variable number of columns.
A table has a variable number of columns. A matrix has a fixed number of columns.
explanation: A table has a fixed column for each field in the columns area. A matrix has a column for the rows area, plus columns for each unique value in the column fields — making its number of columns variable.

choiceExplanations.0: Both tables and matrices can summarise data using aggregation functions (SUM, COUNT, Average, etc.). The ability to summarise data is not what distinguishes them.
choiceExplanations.1: This reverses the actual capabilities. Tables CAN summarise data; matrices also summarise but additionally support row/column pivoting.
choiceExplanations.2: Correct. A table visual has a fixed set of columns — one per field placed in the Columns/Values area. A matrix visual's column count is variable because it generates a column for each unique value in the fields placed in its Columns field well, in addition to the row hierarchy.
choiceExplanations.3: This reverses the correct relationship. A table has a FIXED column count (one column per field added). A matrix has a VARIABLE column count driven by the unique values in its Columns field well.

subtopic: Enhance reports for usability and storytelling
examObjective: Visualize and analyze the data > Configure sync slicers
commonTrap: Confusing Sync Slicers with Edit Interactions
question: A report has an Overview page, a Sales Detail page, and an Inventory Detail page, all built on the same Sales data. The report designer wants a Region slicer placed on the Overview page to also filter the visuals on the other two pages, without duplicating the slicer on each page. Which feature should the designer use?
choices: It allows a single slicer to affect multiple pages.
It allows you to choose which visuals on the same page are affected by the slicer.
It allows you to format the style of the slicer.
explanation: Sync Slicers (View > Sync Slicers) allows a slicer on one page to filter visuals on other pages. You can also control whether the slicer is visible on those other pages.

choiceExplanations.0: Correct. Sync Slicers (View > Sync Slicers) allows a single slicer placed on one page to filter visuals on other pages too, eliminating the need to duplicate the slicer on each page.
choiceExplanations.1: Controlling which visuals on the same page are affected by a slicer is done through Edit Interactions (Format > Edit interactions) — not through Sync Slicers.
choiceExplanations.2: Slicer style formatting (dropdown vs list vs tile, font, colors) is configured in the Format pane — Sync Slicers is exclusively for enabling cross-page slicer behaviour.

subtopic: Enhance reports for usability and storytelling
examObjective: Visualize and analyze the data > Apply slicing and filtering
commonTrap: Thinking slicer affects all pages by default
question: An analyst creates a slicer on a page that already contains 3 other visuals. By default, which visuals does this slicer affect?
choices: The nearest visual to the slicer.
The visuals that you choose in the Format pane.
All visuals on that page.
All visuals in the report (all pages).
explanation: By default, a slicer affects all visuals on the same page. To extend it to other pages, you use View - Sync Slicers.

choiceExplanations.0: By default, a slicer affects ALL visuals on the current page — not just the nearest one. Selective control requires manually editing interactions for each visual.
choiceExplanations.1: The Format pane for a slicer controls its visual appearance (style, font, colors). Selecting which visuals a slicer affects is done through Format > Edit Interactions, not the Format pane.
choiceExplanations.2: Correct. By default, a slicer filters all visuals on the same report page it's placed on. To extend its effect to other pages, View > Sync Slicers must be explicitly enabled.
choiceExplanations.3: Slicers do not affect other pages by default — only the current page. Cross-page syncing requires explicitly configuring View > Sync Slicers.

examObjective: Visualize and analyze the data > Apply slicing and filtering
commonTrap: Confusing ? with * or % wildcard characters
question: An analyst is creating an Advanced Filter on a Product Code column and wants to match codes where exactly one character varies (for example, matching both 'AB1XX' and 'AB2XX' but not 'AB12XX'). Which wildcard represents exactly one character in an Advanced Filter?
explanation: In Advanced Filters, '?' represents exactly one character, and '*' represents zero, one or multiple characters.

choiceExplanations.0: '*' is also valid in Power BI Advanced Filters but represents zero or more characters — not exactly one. Use '?' when you need to match exactly one unknown character.
choiceExplanations.1: '_' is a single-character wildcard in SQL and Excel LIKE expressions but is not recognised in Power BI's Advanced Filter panel, which uses '?' instead.
choiceExplanations.2: Correct. In Power BI's Advanced Filter, '?' is the wildcard that represents exactly one unknown character, so 'AB?XX' matches 'AB1XX' and 'AB2XX' but not the two-character variant 'AB12XX'.
choiceExplanations.3: '%' is the multi-character wildcard used in SQL — it is not used in Power BI's Advanced Filter, which uses '*' for multiple characters.

examObjective: Visualize and analyze the data > Apply slicing and filtering
commonTrap: Using Basic filtering when conditions like 'contains' are needed
question: A report developer goes to View - Filters and sees 'Filters on this visual', 'Filters on this page', and 'Filters on all pages'. The developer wants to add a filter that shows only Region Names containing 'East' or 'Midlands', and the filter should automatically update when the underlying data changes. Which Filter Type should be used?
choices: Basic filtering
Advanced filtering
Top N
Relative date
explanation: Advanced filtering allows conditions such as 'contains', 'greater than', and 'is not blank'. Basic filtering only provides checkboxes for specific values.

choiceExplanations.0: Basic filtering shows a checkbox list of known field values — it does not support text conditions like 'contains' or 'begins with', or combining multiple text conditions.
choiceExplanations.1: Correct. Advanced filtering supports text conditions such as 'contains', allowing a filter like 'Region Name contains East OR contains Midlands' that automatically re-evaluates as the underlying data changes.
choiceExplanations.2: Top N filtering shows only the top or bottom N items by a measure — it cannot apply text-matching conditions like 'contains East'.
choiceExplanations.3: Relative date filtering applies rolling date windows (e.g., 'last 30 days') — it only works on date fields and cannot apply text matching conditions.

subtopic: Enhance reports for usability and storytelling
examObjective: Visualize and analyze the data > Group and layer visuals by using the Selection pane
commonTrap: Going to Format pane instead of Selection pane
question: A report designer wants to temporarily hide a visual on the report canvas — without deleting it — so it can be shown again later via a bookmark or button action. Which pane should they use to hide the visual?
choices: The Format pane
The Bookmarks pane
The Sync Slicers pane
The Selection pane
explanation: The Selection pane (View > Selection) allows you to hide visuals, change their layer order, and manage tab order for accessibility.

choiceExplanations.0: The Format pane controls visual appearance — colors, fonts, borders — but does not have a visibility toggle. Hiding a visual requires the Selection pane.
choiceExplanations.1: The Bookmarks pane records and manages saved report states. While bookmarks can capture a visual's hidden state, you use the Selection pane to actually toggle visibility.
choiceExplanations.2: The Sync Slicers pane manages cross-page slicer synchronisation — it has no visual visibility controls.
choiceExplanations.3: Correct. The Selection pane (View > Selection) lets you toggle a visual's visibility off without deleting it, so it can be revealed later via a bookmark or button action.

subtopic: Enhance reports for usability and storytelling
examObjective: Visualize and analyze the data > Configure bookmarks
commonTrap: Thinking bookmarks save the data source
question: A report designer is using bookmarks to capture different filter and visual states for a guided walkthrough of a sales report. A colleague asks whether switching to a different bookmark could also redirect the report to a different underlying data source. Which of the following is NOT something that bookmarks save or control?
choices: Save data sources
Save filter, drill and sort state
Save visual display state
Save the current page
explanation: Bookmarks capture the state of a report page including filters, visuals, slicers, and page visibility — but they do NOT save data sources.

choiceExplanations.0: Correct. Bookmarks capture the visual state of a report page — filters, sort order, drill state, visual visibility, and the current page — but they do not store or switch the underlying data source connection.
choiceExplanations.1: Saving filter, drill, and sort state IS something bookmarks do — capturing the current filter context is one of their primary purposes.
choiceExplanations.2: Saving visual display state (visible/hidden, cross-highlight selections) IS something bookmarks do — this enables show/hide navigation patterns in reports.
choiceExplanations.3: Capturing which report page is currently displayed IS something bookmarks do — this is what enables page navigation buttons when bookmarks are combined with button actions.

examObjective: Visualize and analyze the data > Format and configure visuals
commonTrap: Putting the field in Legend instead of Small multiples
question: A stacked bar chart visual needs to be changed so that, instead of showing a single chart, it shows multiple small charts — one for each Department. Where should the Department field be placed?
choices: In the Y-axis area
In the Legend area
In the Small multiples area
In the Tooltips area
explanation: Dragging a field into the Small multiples area creates a separate chart for each value of that field. Legend would color-code within a single chart.

choiceExplanations.0: Placing Department in the Y-axis makes departments the Y-axis categories within a single chart — all departments appear as separate bars in one chart, not as separate small charts.
choiceExplanations.1: The Legend field color-codes data points by category within a single chart — placing Department in Legend creates colored series within one chart, not separate charts per department.
choiceExplanations.2: Correct. Placing Department in the Small multiples well splits the single stacked bar chart into a grid of separate mini-charts, one per department, each showing the same measures and axes.
choiceExplanations.3: The Tooltips field adds data shown on hover over a data point — it does not create separate chart instances for each category value.

subtopic: Enhance reports for usability and storytelling
examObjective: Visualize and analyze the data > Apply sorting to visuals
commonTrap: Looking for a dedicated Sort button or going to View menu
question: A report developer wants to sort data in descending order within a visual. How can this be achieved?
choices: Click on the ↓ down arrow next to a visual.
Click on the ... next to a visual
Go to View - Sort.
Go to the Format pane.
explanation: To sort a visual, click on the '...' (more options) icon next to the visual, then go to Sort by to change the sort field and direction.

choiceExplanations.0: There is no standard '↓ down arrow' sort control directly visible on a visual in Power BI. Sort direction and field are accessed via the '...' more options menu.
choiceExplanations.1: Correct. Clicking the '...' (more options) icon on a visual opens a menu that includes 'Sort by', where you can choose the sort field and toggle ascending/descending order.
choiceExplanations.2: 'View > Sort' is not a valid menu path in Power BI Desktop. Sorting is controlled per-visual through the visual's own '...' more options menu.
choiceExplanations.3: The Format pane controls visual appearance and has no sort direction or sort field controls.

subtopic: Enhance reports for usability and storytelling
examObjective: Visualize and analyze the data > Configure navigation for a report
commonTrap: Looking in Insert - Shapes instead of Insert - Buttons
question: A report designer has created several bookmarks representing different views of a sales report and now wants to add a set of buttons that let users step through these bookmarks in sequence. Where should they go to add this bookmark navigator?
choices: In the Home menu - you can insert it like any visual.
In the Insert menu - Buttons
In the Insert menu - Shapes
In the Modeling menu
explanation: A bookmark navigator is found under Insert > Buttons. It creates a button group that navigates between bookmarks.

choiceExplanations.0: The Home tab's visual gallery contains standard chart and data visuals — bookmark navigators are navigation elements found under Insert > Buttons, not in the visual gallery.
choiceExplanations.1: Correct. The bookmark navigator is a button group inserted via Insert > Buttons, which automatically generates Previous/Next-style controls that step through the report's saved bookmarks in order.
choiceExplanations.2: Insert > Shapes adds decorative shapes (rectangles, circles, lines) — interactive navigation elements like bookmark navigators are under Insert > Buttons.
choiceExplanations.3: The Modeling menu contains DAX calculation tools and relationship management — it does not contain UI navigation elements like buttons or bookmark navigators.

subtopic: Enhance reports for usability and storytelling
examObjective: Visualize and analyze the data > Configure navigation for a report
commonTrap: Thinking Text Boxes support Action types like Buttons do
question: Using the 'on-object interaction' feature, which of the following ways can I NOT insert something that will allow the user to run a Q&A?
choices: Go to the Home menu and, in the Insert drop-down box, under AI visuals, click on Q&A.
Go to Insert and add a Text Box. In the Format pane for the Text Box, change the 'Action' to Q&A.
Go to Insert menu and click on Q&A.
Go to Insert and click on Buttons, and then click on Q&A.
explanation: Text Boxes do not have an 'Action' option in their Format pane. Only Buttons, Shapes, and Images support Actions. Therefore, a Text Box cannot be configured to launch Q&A.

choiceExplanations.0: You CAN insert a Q&A visual from Home > Insert dropdown under AI visuals — this is a valid method for adding Q&A to a report page.
choiceExplanations.1: Correct. Text Boxes do not expose an 'Action' property in the Format pane, so a Text Box cannot be configured to launch Q&A — unlike Buttons, Shapes, and Images, which all support Actions including Q&A.
choiceExplanations.2: You CAN insert Q&A from the Insert menu directly — this is a standard, valid approach.
choiceExplanations.3: You CAN configure a Button with Q&A as its action type via Insert > Buttons — this creates a clickable Q&A launcher button.

subtopic: Enhance reports for usability and storytelling
examObjective: Visualize and analyze the data > Configure navigation for a report
commonTrap: Thinking Sync Slicers is a button action
question: A report designer is configuring a button's Action property to help users navigate a multi-page report. While reviewing the available options, which of the following is NOT a valid Action that can be assigned to a button?
choices: Back
Bookmark
Q&A
Sync slicers
explanation: Valid Actions for buttons include: Back, Bookmark, Drill through, Page navigation, Q&A, and Web URL. Sync Slicers is a View menu feature, not a button action.

choiceExplanations.0: 'Back' IS a valid button action — it navigates to the previously viewed report page.
choiceExplanations.1: 'Bookmark' IS a valid button action — it applies a specific saved bookmark state when clicked.
choiceExplanations.2: 'Q&A' IS a valid button action — it opens the Q&A natural language interface.
choiceExplanations.3: Correct. 'Sync slicers' is not an available Action type for buttons — it is a page-level View menu feature for synchronising slicer selections across pages, not something a button can trigger.

subtopic: Enhance reports for usability and storytelling
examObjective: Visualize and analyze the data > Configure drillthrough navigation
commonTrap: Confusing drill-through with drill-down within a visual
question: A sales report has a summary page showing revenue by region. When a user clicks on a specific region bar, they need to navigate to a separate page that shows only the individual store transactions for that region. Which Power BI feature directly supports this interaction pattern?
choices: Drill down within the same visual — the X-axis changes from Region to Store without leaving the visual
Drillthrough — right-clicking a data point on the source page passes its filter context to a dedicated detail page
Drill up — a button that expands the visual hierarchy from regions to stores within the same chart
Page navigation buttons — static buttons that always navigate to the detail page regardless of which region is selected
explanation: Drillthrough enables navigation from one report page to another while passing the filter context of the selected data point. The destination page applies that context automatically — in this case, filtering all visuals to the selected region. Drill down (A) and drill up (C) operate within the same visual hierarchy without leaving the page. Page navigation buttons (D) are static and navigate to the same destination regardless of selection, without passing filter context.

choiceExplanations.0: Changing the X-axis from Years to Quarters within the same visual is 'drill-down' — it navigates within a hierarchy inside one visual, not across report pages.
choiceExplanations.1: Correct. Drill-through lets a user right-click a data point on a summary page and jump to a separate, filtered detail page — navigating between pages, rather than changing hierarchy levels within a single visual.
choiceExplanations.2: Expanding to show both Years and sub-levels simultaneously within the same visual is 'Expand all down one level' — a hierarchy expansion that operates within a single visual.
choiceExplanations.3: Focusing on one selected year and then showing its quarters within the same visual is also drill-down behavior — it operates within a single visual's hierarchy, not navigating to another page.

examObjective: Visualize and analyze the data > Format and configure visuals
commonTrap: Putting SalesVolume into the Y Axis instead of Size
question: A scatter chart needs to be changed into a bubble chart so that bubbles appear larger when SalesVolume is higher and smaller when SalesVolume is lower. Where should the SalesVolume field be placed?
choices: Into the Size section.
Into the Area section.
Into the Y Axis.
Into the Legend.
explanation: In a scatter/bubble chart, the Size field controls the size of each bubble. Placing SalesVolume in Size means higher values produce larger bubbles.

choiceExplanations.0: Correct. In a scatter/bubble chart, dragging SalesVolume into the Size field well controls the diameter of each bubble — higher values render as larger bubbles, lower values as smaller ones.
choiceExplanations.1: 'Area' is not a named field well in Power BI's scatter/bubble chart. Bubble size is controlled exclusively by the 'Size' field.
choiceExplanations.2: The Y Axis field sets the vertical position of each bubble based on that measure's value — it does not control the size of the bubble.
choiceExplanations.3: The Legend field assigns different colors to bubbles based on a category — it has no effect on bubble size.

examObjective: Visualize and analyze the data > Format and configure visuals
commonTrap: Putting Year in the Time Axis instead of Play Axis
question: A scatter chart needs to be animated to show results for individual years. Where should the Year field be placed?
choices: In the Time Axis.
In the Play Axis.
In the Breakdown Axis.
In the Legend.
explanation: The Play Axis in a scatter chart enables animation. When a field is placed in the Play Axis, you can click the Play button to animate the chart across each value (e.g., year).

choiceExplanations.0: 'Time Axis' is not the name of any field well in Power BI's scatter chart. The animation field is specifically called 'Play Axis'.
choiceExplanations.1: Correct. Placing Year in the Play Axis field well enables the chart's animation control, letting users click Play to step through (or animate) the scatter chart one year at a time.
choiceExplanations.2: 'Breakdown Axis' is used in waterfall charts to show individual category contributions — it is not a field section in scatter charts.
choiceExplanations.3: The Legend field color-codes scatter points by category — it does not animate the chart across time periods.

examObjective: Visualize and analyze the data > Format and configure visuals
commonTrap: Going to Format pane to deselect Cumulative Total instead of using Breakdown
question: A waterfall chart currently displays a cumulative total. A report developer needs it to show each category individually instead. What change should be made?
choices: Add a field to the Category area.
Add a field to the Y-axis area.
Add a field to the Breakdown area.
Go to the Format pane, to the Totals section, and deselect 'Cumulative Total'.
explanation: In a waterfall chart, adding a field to the Breakdown area shows each category separately rather than as a running cumulative total.

choiceExplanations.0: The Category area defines the X-axis groups in the waterfall chart — adding another field there creates a second grouping dimension, not a switch from cumulative to individual display.
choiceExplanations.1: The Y-axis area holds the measure being visualised — changing the measure does not control whether values appear cumulatively or individually.
choiceExplanations.2: Correct. Adding a field to the Breakdown well in a waterfall chart splits the total into individual category contributions, replacing the single cumulative bar with separate increase/decrease bars per category.
choiceExplanations.3: There is no 'Cumulative Total' toggle in the waterfall chart's Format pane Totals section. The Breakdown field well is the correct mechanism for showing individual category contributions.

examObjective: Visualize and analyze the data > Create reports
commonTrap: Confusing AppSource with PowerBI.com marketplace
question: A report designer wants to add a custom visual that is not included in the default Power BI Desktop visuals to enhance a dashboard. From which marketplace can additional custom visuals be downloaded?
choices: PowerBICenter
AppSource
VisualStudio
AnalysisStore
explanation: Custom Power BI visuals are downloaded from Microsoft AppSource. You can access it directly from the Visualization pane in Power BI Desktop.

choiceExplanations.0: 'PowerBICenter' is not a real Microsoft service — it does not exist. Microsoft AppSource is the only official marketplace for Power BI custom visuals.
choiceExplanations.1: Correct. Microsoft AppSource is the official marketplace for Power BI custom visuals, and it can be browsed directly from the 'Get more visuals' option in the Visualization pane.
choiceExplanations.2: Visual Studio is Microsoft's IDE for writing software code — it is not a marketplace for Power BI custom visuals.
choiceExplanations.3: 'AnalysisStore' is not a real Microsoft service. The correct marketplace is Microsoft AppSource.

examObjective: Visualize and analyze the data > Select an appropriate visual
commonTrap: Confusing conversion rate with completion rate
question: A funnel chart shows that 100% of users start the first process, but only 71.5% complete the last process. What is this percentage called?
choices: The conversion rate
The success rate
The completion rate
The checkout rate
explanation: The conversion rate in a funnel chart represents the percentage of users who complete the entire process from start to finish.

choiceExplanations.0: Correct. In a Power BI funnel chart, the percentage of users who make it from the first stage all the way through to the last stage is labelled the conversion rate.
choiceExplanations.1: 'Success rate' is a general-purpose term for positive outcomes — it is not the specific terminology Power BI uses for the funnel's start-to-finish completion percentage.
choiceExplanations.2: 'Completion rate' could describe the same concept informally but is not the standard label Power BI's funnel visual uses — it specifically calls this the 'conversion rate'.
choiceExplanations.3: 'Checkout rate' is e-commerce jargon for purchase flow completion — it is not the generic Power BI funnel visual terminology.

examObjective: Visualize and analyze the data > Format and configure visuals
commonTrap: Thinking the Category and Details sections behave identically for color assignment
question: A treemap is created with RegionName in the Category section. A developer wants to add the Year field to either the Category or the Details section. Which of the following statements is true about the color behavior?
choices: If Year is in either section, all rectangles for a particular RegionName will be different colors.
If Year is in either section, all rectangles for a particular RegionName will be the same color.
If Year is in the Category section, rectangles for the same RegionName will be the same color. If Year is in the Details section, they will be different colors.
If Year is in the Category section, rectangles for the same RegionName will be different colors. If Year is in the Details section, they will be the same color.
explanation: In a treemap, fields in the Category section define color groupings. Adding Year to Category makes each Year a separate color group. Fields in the Details section break categories into sub-rectangles but share the parent category color.

choiceExplanations.0: Color grouping behavior differs based on which field well you use — Category and Details behave differently for color assignment. Both sections do not result in all-different colors per region.
choiceExplanations.1: Colors are not the same in either case — Category reassigns the color grouping; Details inherits the parent's color. They have opposite behaviors.
choiceExplanations.2: This reverses the correct behavior. Adding Year to Category makes Year the color-defining dimension (different years = different colors within the same region). Adding Year to Details keeps RegionName as the color group (all a region's rectangles share the same color).
choiceExplanations.3: Correct. Adding Year to the Category section makes Year the color-defining field, so rectangles for the same RegionName appear in different colors per year. Adding Year to the Details section keeps RegionName as the color group, so all of a region's rectangles share the same color regardless of year.

subtopic: Design and implement a data model
examObjective: Model the data > Configure table and column properties
commonTrap: Looking in Report view Field pane or Modeling menu
question: A hierarchy of Country - City - State has been created in the wrong order. The 'City' level needs to be moved down. Where should this change be made?
choices: In the Report view, I go to the Field pane.
In the Report view, I go to the Modeling menu.
In the Data view, I go to the Data pane.
In the Model view, I click on the table and go to the Properties pane.
explanation: To reorder levels in a hierarchy, go to Model view, click on the table containing the hierarchy, find it in the Properties pane, and drag the levels to reorder them. Click 'Apply Level Changes' to confirm.

choiceExplanations.0: The Fields pane in Report view lets you drag fields into visuals and expand tables — it does not provide drag-to-reorder functionality for hierarchy levels.
choiceExplanations.1: The Modeling menu in Report view contains DAX calculation tools and relationship settings — it does not have a user interface for reordering hierarchy levels.
choiceExplanations.2: The Data view shows table row data and allows column-level property changes via Column tools — hierarchies cannot be reordered from the Data pane in this view.
choiceExplanations.3: Correct. Hierarchy levels are reordered in Model view by selecting the table that contains the hierarchy, opening the Properties pane, and dragging the levels into the desired order, then applying the level changes.

subtopic: Design and implement a data model
examObjective: Model the data > Configure table and column properties
